title: KV coherency, eviction patterns, prefix-reuse and batch-latency playbook - NovaQuant deep dive
summary: Deep technical troubleshooting session focusing on KV cache coherency, eviction/paging behavior under long-context workloads and the interaction with batching and quantization. Agreed set of telemetry captures and a pilot load test to reproduce eviction hotspots; Redwood to deliver dashboards and a prioritized tuning playbook.
topics: KV cache eviction behavior under mixed prefix workloads
Batching impact on latency and tail latency
Private/VPC deployment considerations for KV persistence
Telemetry signals and synthetic load test plan
action_items: Alex Mercer: Share current KV telemetry dashboard (Grafana link) and the eviction-rate query by 2026-06-13
Priya Desai: Produce a short 'playbook' of 5 tuning knobs (prefetch, batch sizing, kv-ttl, hot-prefix sharding, quantization profile) by 2026-06-15
Omar Reyes: Provide sample request traces and SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) and the peak QPS expected for the pilot by 2026-06-14
Hannah Kim: Run small on-prem benchmark with their long-context prompt set and upload raw telemetry (cpu/gpu/kb/s) by 2026-06-18
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff (synthetic load) next week - tentative 2026-06-17
Redwood to share security docs for VPC/private deployment in parallel
Customer to confirm list of stakeholders for pilot and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. today we want to go deep on your kv behavior, eviction hotspots and how batching is affecting tail latency. um, priya and i will drive the tech bits.
[00:18] Dana: thanks, alex. quick context — we run an assistant that holds 40k token histories for some clients, but we see periodic latency spikes and also token hallucination increases after long sessions. suspect kv misses and paging to disk, maybe quantization noise.
[00:35] Priya: got it. can you share the workload profile — distribution of sequence lengths and prefix reuse? even coarse numbers help.
[00:42] Hannah: sure; roughly 20% short queries (<512), 60% medium (512-4k), 20% long (4k-40k). prefix reuse is high for support flows (same convo ids), but search workflows have low prefix reuse and generate a lot of distinct keys.
[01:05] Omar: we run private cluster on prem, NVMe backed. we use the default kv-ttl of 12 hours. during bursts we see spikes in IO and some requests time out at our gateway.
[01:18] Alex: ok that fits a prefetch / eviction capacity mismatch — when many unique prefixes come in, the kv store thrashes. two paths: increase kv capacity (memory) or tune prefetch heuristics and eviction policy.
[01:35] Priya: quick note — our runtime does continuous batching and kv prefix caching. by default it uses an LRU-ish eviction with a shadow TTL and a prefetch window that targets active prefixes. but in high cardinality prefix patterns LRU degenerates and you get frequent spill/paging.
[01:55] Dana: are we seeing wrong prefixes e.g. prefix aliasing or collisions? we thought our conversation ids were unique.
[02:03] Priya: collisions are rare; more common is prefix churn — many near-unique prefixes that share early tokens so caches keep thrashing the same slots. also hot prefixes can become victims if sharding isn't hotspot-aware.
[02:20] Alex: we should instrument 'prefix heat' — a metric that counts reuse rate per prefix over sliding window. couple that with eviction latency and miss penalty. right now we look at global hit rate which hides hotspots.
[02:37] Hannah: we do have per-request ids in logs, can we attach those to telemetry?
[02:41] Priya: yes, please include convo_id and prefix_hash. we'll provide a recommended tagging schema.
[02:47] [00:03:00] Omar: about paging — our NVMe isn't saturated generally, but during sustained 300 qps with many long context requests we hit 95% utilization and io wait increases. that aligns with the timeouts.
[03:15] Alex: that's classic spillover. eviction writes + reads create IO storms. two mitigations: 1) increase async prefetch so most likely prefixes are resident, 2) change eviction policy to avoid evicting the hot-slot during re-shard windows.
[03:32] Priya: also consider 'eviction hysteresis' — don't evict a prefix until it's been cold for X seconds; combined with write-behind batching reduces churn. default is 2s in hosted, but for your traffic maybe 8-12s.
[03:48] Dana: increasing kv-ttl would help but memory cost is a concern. any guidance on sizing memory vs expected hit rate?
[03:56] Alex: yes — Priya has an equation: required mem ≈ sum_over_prefixes(avg_kv_size * active_prefix_count). but practical approach: capture per-prefix size histogram, then simulate LRU at target cache size to estimate hit rate. we can run that for you.
[04:12] Priya: and we have a tool that replays traces and simulates eviction — we can run it against your recent logs to get a recommended cache size.
[04:22] Hannah: nice. what about batching? our engineers noted that increasing batch size reduced avg latency but p99 got worse.
[04:30] Priya: yes, batching trades latency for throughput and can increase queuing, amplifying tail latency when KV misses cause a slow path. big batches hold KV locks longer depending on runtime. tune batching adaptively: smaller batches on tail pressure, larger at steady-state.
[04:46] Alex: also ensure batching boundaries align with prefix locality — if a batch mixes many different prefixes it causes the runtime to fetch many distinct KV sets concurrently, increasing IO. prefer prefix-aware batching when possible.
[05:02] Omar: is prefix-aware batching something Redwood runtime supports today?
[05:06] Priya: partially. planned improvements: group-by-prefix windowing and soft-affinity within the batcher. current workaround: use affinity sharding at ingress (sticky routing by convo id) so batches naturally have higher reuse.
[05:22] Dana: routing by convo id might be hard with our load balancer. we prefer a platform-level fix.
[05:29] Alex: understood — for the pilot we'll test two approaches: 1) increase prefetch + hysteresis and run the synthetic burst, 2) run affinity sharding in a canary path for a small percent of traffic to measure effect.
[05:44] Hannah: quantization — we moved to int8 for cost. we see occasional divergence in long-context outputs. could kv misses worsen quantization artifacts?
[05:53] Priya: quantization mainly affects model numeric stability. KV cache interactions affect which tokens are requested and their order; if a miss causes re-computation on a different quantized kernel path, you could see small diffs that amplify over long contexts. the mitigation: pick a quantization profile with better long-sequence fidelity (bfloat or per-channel) and pin that for the long-context model variant.
[06:18] Omar: for on-prem, is KV persistence recommended? we have intermittent node restarts for maintenance and we'd like some warm-start to avoid cold misses.
[06:28] Alex: persistence can help. options: local snapshotting of most-hot prefixes to disk, or a small distributed backbone with replication factor 2 to reduce cold-starts. downside is write amplification. For VPC/private we can offer a managed fallback to Redwood Dedicated for the cold path.
[06:48] Priya: also consider warmup heuristics on deploy — prefetch top N hot prefixes after restart. we can provide a prewarm script that consumes your top-100 prefixes list.
[06:58] Dana: telemetry — what exact signals do you want for the pilot?
[07:02] Priya: minimal set: per-prefix hit rate, per-prefix size, eviction_timestamp, eviction_reason (ttl/space/hot_eviction), io_wait_ms, nvme_util_percent, batch_size_distribution, batch_prefix_entropy, quantization_profile_inuse, model_variant. add request-level p50/p95/p99 and trace id.
[07:25] Alex: we'll send a sample dashboard and the wire format for logs. please ensure timestamps are UTC and convo ids are consistent.
[07:33] [00:07:40] Omar: about security — we'll need SSO and audit logs. is the KV telemetry sanitized?
[07:41] Priya: yes — we recommend hashing convo ids and stripping PII in telemetry. Redwood supports KMS integration for any telemetry storage in private deployments.
[07:53] Hannah: one more thing — when we tried increasing kv-ttl we saw mem thrash elsewhere, like session-store. could there be cross-cache interference?
[08:02] Alex: possible. if caches share the same host memory pool or the OS page cache, increasing one cache shifts pressure to others and can trigger swap. for on-prem tune cgroup memory limits and ensure dedicated GPUs don't share host memory pages.
[08:20] Priya: we also recommend isolating kv into its own storage class or use container memory reservation to avoid cross-talk.
[08:27] Dana: ok, what's the pilot success criteria?
[08:30] Alex: reduction in p99 latency by at least 30% during peak, eviction rate down by 50% for top-1k prefixes, and no increase in hallucination/error rate on long prompts.
[08:43] Omar: those are measurable. we'll provide baseline metrics.
[08:47] Priya: timeline: telemetry handoff by Friday, Redwood runs trace simulation over the weekend, pilot kickoff Wed next week, 48-hour synthetic burst and analysis.
[08:58] Alex: any other blockers?
[09:00] Dana: just internal approvals for debug logs sharing; should be fine.
[09:05] Hannah: i'll compile the prompt set and attach to the ticket.
[09:09] Alex: great. recap: Redwood sends dashboards + playbook; NovaQuant shares traces and SLOs; run pilot; follow-up 2026-06-19 for results.
[09:21] Dana: thanks everyone.
[09:23] [END]
